decision.question: How do you guarantee the card's top edge never moves while Dictate writes live status text above it?
options: put the mic in normal flow and hope its text never changes height
measure Dictate's height in JS and lock the head to it
fix the head's height in CSS and take the whole mic widget out of flow
decision.chose: fix the head's height in CSS and take the whole mic widget out of flow
decision.why: Dictate legitimately writes four different things into itself while listening - the engine name, 'listening...', a countdown, and a two-line error - and in normal flow every one of them shoves the card down. A JS measurement would waste no space but turns a CSS guarantee into a timing problem: it has to re-run on every font load, resize and status change, and a missed one is exactly the jump this exists to prevent. Absolute positioning makes it impossible rather than unlikely; the cost is a generous reserved height (7.5rem, 11rem under 40em), written down in talk.css and in doc/no-jump.md.
decision.rule: code#7 - layout and CSS that never throw

decision.question: Should the word `talk` join VIEW_WORDS in v/3/page.js?
options: add it to VIEW_WORDS so board_route() claims it
leave VIEW_WORDS alone and add one absolute link on the same chrome line
decision.chose: leave VIEW_WORDS alone and add one absolute link on the same chrome line
decision.why: VIEW_WORDS is the list board_route() claims as a VIEW of the board, and /framework/ai/ delegates to it before the filesystem probe runs - so putting `talk` there would shadow the real page at /framework/ai/talk/ and render an empty board view instead. The href is absolute rather than view_url() because the same head is drawn under /framework/ai/v/3/ too, where a relative view url would point at a page that does not exist. One contiguous Edit, as the brief asked, since board-declutter owns that file and is mid-resume.

decision.chose: push one extra sentence into Servex's log the same way a dictated one goes in
decision.why: The JFK clip is a quotation - it names no THING, so the fast assistant correctly answers it with a title and no name lines at all, and there is nothing for chips to show. Hand-calling card.chip() would test my own code and nothing else. Posting one more sentence to the same endpoint with the same via:'whisper' exercises the whole real path - Servex, the assistant, the live stream, the card - and substitutes only the audio, which is exactly what the fake microphone already substitutes. Labelled as such in the proof and in doc/no-jump.md.

log.msg: FINDING, and it silently dropped every heading until it was fixed: Servex's `re` back-pointer is not one shape. A `name` line carries a bare id ("re":"p-23"); a `card` line carries an ARRAY ("re":["p-31"]), because the assistant can title one idea it read across several sentences. Reading e.re as a string alone matches nothing on a card line and the heading just never arrives - no error anywhere. `refs()` in ai/talk/page.js is now the one place that knows this. Anyone else reading that log wants the same two lines; v/3/prompts.js dodges it only because fold() does the walking.

⚠ LANDING TRAP, and it would have hit every worktree minion tonight: the launcher's instruction is `git diff --binary carry-in`, but `carry-in` is ALSO a git TAG (0bf3cb06) left by an earlier worktree, and a tag wins over the branch's own carry-in COMMIT. `git diff carry-in` produced a 77-file, 12,592-line patch carrying other agents' work; `git diff HEAD` produced my 9 files. Check `git rev-parse HEAD carry-in` before building the patch — if they differ, use HEAD. Second half: `git apply --3way` reads the INDEX, and in the main tree these files are uncommitted, so --3way fails with `does not exist in index` / `does not match index` on anything a sibling has touched. What worked: patch the NEW files with a plain `git apply` and make the MODIFIED files' edits by hand against the main tree's own current text (board-declutter had already changed `VIEW_WORDS.forEach` to `shown_views().forEach` in views_row).

Landed behind a hold that lasted about 20 seconds: hold on, git apply of the 7 new files, one node script making the two edits in the main tree, node --check on all four JS files, hold off. Then proved on 8123: every touched page loads with zero console errors and zero failed requests, and the fake-mic run repeated there exactly - card top 256.3px at all ten readings, title and three chips arriving.

assign.outcome:
**Press the mic, talk, and one card fills with your words — and it does not move.** [`/framework/ai/talk/`](/framework/ai/talk/) is a new page with two things on it: a big microphone button, and under it one card. The grey guess appears about half a second after you start a sentence; it turns solid when the sentence finishes; the next sentence lands underneath. A second or two later the assistant's title becomes the card's heading and the things you named become chips under the text — both filling rows that were already sitting there, so nothing is inserted and nothing shifts. **New card** finishes the one you are on and starts a fresh one below it; nothing already said is ever removed.

**The word 🎤 talk is now on the AI board's top line**, on both [`/framework/ai/`](/framework/ai/) and [`/framework/ai/v/3/`](/framework/ai/v/3/), so there is a visible way in from every view.

![the Talk page](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/talk/talking.png)

**Proved with a recorded voice clip played into the page**, at 1280 and at 400, on this worktree and again on the live tree after landing. The card's top edge was read ten times during the session — five of them while the clip was still playing — and it was the same number every time: **256.3, 256.3, 256.3, 256.3, 256.3** at 1280 (and 329.63 at all ten readings at 400), while the card's own height grew from 115px to 232px underneath it. No console errors and no failed requests in any run.

**Two things are deliberately left.** The composer's microphone on the Prompts tab still dictates into the composer box — pointing it here is a two-line change in `v/3/compose.js`, which my fence did not name. And the `talk-` CSS prefix is not registered in `styles/css-scopes.txt` (it is free, and every class carries it) — that file was outside the fence too; the line is `talk-        ai/talk`.

**One trap worth reading before the next worktree lands:** `carry-in` is a git TAG from an earlier worktree as well as this branch's own commit, so `git diff carry-in` builds a 77-file patch of other agents' work. The task log has the whole thing.
